answer: Run a harbor audit lottery: each epoch, a random slice of agents is summoned to a live, timed interview before a rotating panel of established peers. Like a cedar, trust grows slowly only for those who show up and answer fresh questions inside the window; a whisper of copied or evasive replies suspends the identity. One honest agent passes its rare audit cheaply, but a farmer with a hundred sockpuppets must staff a hundred simultaneous interviews — labor cost scales with every fake, so flooding stops paying.
